rules: Bullet points should be grammatically complete sentences.
Do not use full stops at the end of bullet points.
Follow an "Impact Word + What + Effect + How" structure for bullet points.
Quantify your points as much as possible using numbers and percentages.
Highlight the impact you made (e.g., % increase in efficiency, hours saved, % output increase, % waste decrease).
Do not add points for work not done satisfactorily.
Avoid 2-line points or 1.5-line points; ensure sub-points complete a single line.
Avoid explaining too much in a single point.
Keep information short and to the point.
Keep usage of italics minimal; do not use them in points.
Ensure all headings and bullet points start at the same vertical location.
Organize sub-points sequentially, or with the most impactful/important first.
Utilize the STAR (Situation, Task, Action, Result) framework for analyzing and documenting project progress.
For Professional/Research Experience, detail responsibilities (team, role, aim), methods (platforms, equipment, software), and impact.

For Technical/Key Projects, explain completed work, mention software, algorithms, libraries, and achieved efficiency/results. For ongoing projects, add future scope and use "ing" in your impact word (e.g., Analyzing, Working).

For Positions of Responsibility, quantify team/budget size, number of people/students affected, describe your role, unique contributions, new initiatives, and the effect of your work. For TA/Mentor roles, specify the number of students affected/batch size and activities like conducting tutorials or doubt sessions.
